questions.question: In the maximum flow LP, each edge flow $x_{ij}$ is a continuous variable with $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$, where $c_{ij}$ is the capacity of directed edge $(i,j)$. Why is no binary variable needed to decide whether an edge is used?
options: An edge that carries flow is always filled to its capacity.
Unused edges are removed from the network beforehand.
The continuous flows are rounded to 0 or 1 afterwards.
An edge may carry any amount from 0 up to its capacity.

questions.question: The maximum flow LP imposes conservation $\sum_jx_{ji}=\sum_jx_{ij}$ only at vertices $i\ne s,t$, where $s$ is the source (only outgoing edges) and $t$ the sink (only incoming edges). What would imposing it at $s$ as well do?
options: Nothing, as the bounds already balance $s$
Make the LP unbounded, as $s$ has no limit
Force the total flow out of $s$ to be zero
Double the flow value by counting $s$ twice

questions.question: In the maximum flow LP with source $s$ (only outgoing edges), sink $t$ (only incoming edges) and objective $\max\sum_jx_{sj}$, which other objective has the same optimal value?
options: $\max\sum_jc_{sj}$, the capacity out of $s$
$\max\sum_jx_{js}$, summing the flows that enter $s$
$\max\sum_{i\ne s,t}\sum_jx_{ij}$, flow out of middle vertices
$\max\sum_ix_{it}$, the total flow into $t$

questions.question: A maximum flow LP has constraints $\sum_jx_{ji}=\sum_jx_{ij}$ for intermediate vertices $i$ and $0\le x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$ for every directed edge, with capacities $c_{ij}\ge0$. Why does it always have a feasible solution?
options: Setting every $x_{ij}=0$ satisfies all constraints.
Every network contains a path from $s$ to $t$.
The objective is bounded by the capacity out of $s$.
Capacities are always chosen to balance each vertex.

questions.question: In the maximum flow LP for a directed network with source $s$ and sink $t$, what does the decision variable $x_{ij}$ denote?
options: The amount of flow on directed edge $(i,j)$
Whether edge $(i,j)$ is used (1) or not (0)
The capacity available on edge $(i,j)$
The total flow from $i$ to $j$ along any route

questions.question: In a maximum flow network, intermediate vertex $C$ has incoming edges $(A,C)$ and $(B,C)$ and outgoing edges $(C,D)$ and $(C,E)$. Which constraint does the maximum flow LP impose at $C$?
options: $x_{AC}+x_{BC}=x_{CD}+x_{CE}$
$x_{AC}+x_{CD}=x_{BC}+x_{CE}$
$x_{AC}+x_{BC}\le x_{CD}+x_{CE}$

questions.question: A directed network has vertices $s$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $t$ and 8 edges, with source $s$ and sink $t$. How many conservation equations does its maximum flow LP contain?

A network has edges $(s,a)$ with capacity 3, $(s,b)$ 2, $(a,b)$ 2, $(a,t)$ 2 and $(b,t)$ 3. A proposed solution of its maximum flow LP is $x_{sa}=3$, $x_{sb}=2$, $x_{ab}=0$, $x_{at}=3$, $x_{bt}=2$. Which constraint does it violate?
options: Conservation at vertex $a$
Conservation at vertex $b$
None, the solution is feasible
Capacity bound of edge $(a,t)$

questions.question: In a network with edges $(s,a)$, $(s,b)$, $(a,b)$, $(a,t)$ and $(b,t)$, a feasible solution of the maximum flow LP has $x_{sa}=4$, $x_{sb}=1$, $x_{ab}=2$, $x_{at}=2$ and $x_{bt}=3$. What is its objective value?
A pipeline network has a one-way pipe from $B$ to $C$ that can carry at most 4 units. Which constraint on $x_{BC}$ belongs in the maximum flow LP?
options: $0\le x_{BC}\le4$
$-4\le x_{BC}\le4$
$x_{BC}\le4$ only

questions.question: In the maximum flow LP, the source $s$ has only outgoing and the sink $t$ only incoming edges. What does adding the conservation equations of all intermediate vertices show?
options: Every edge carries the same amount of flow.
The flow value equals the total capacity of all edges.
Flow out of $s$ always equals flow into $t$.
Flow out of $s$ is at most the flow into $t$.

questions.question: A maximum flow LP has only integer capacities $c_{ij}$. Which statement about integer-valued optimal flows is correct?
options: Every optimal solution has all flows integral.
Some optimal solution has all flows integral.
Any LP with integer data has an integral optimum.
Integral flows require integer or binary variables.

questions.question: In a maximum flow network, intermediate vertex $b$ is a station that can handle at most 5 units in total. Which constraint added to the maximum flow LP models this?
options: $x_{jb}\le5$ for each edge into $b$
$\sum_jx_{jb}=5$, total inflow into $b$
$\sum_jx_{jb}\le5$, total inflow into $b$
A binary variable that switches $b$ on or off

questions.question: A network has edges $(s,a)$ with capacity 5, $(s,b)$ 4, $(a,b)$ 1, $(a,t)$ 3 and $(b,t)$ 7, with source $s$ and sink $t$. What is the optimal value of its maximum flow LP?

A network has edges $(s,a)$ with capacity 4, $(s,b)$ 3, $(a,b)$ 2, $(a,t)$ 2 and $(b,t)$ 4. A feasible flow has $x_{sa}=4$, $x_{sb}=2$, $x_{ab}=2$, $x_{at}=2$, $x_{bt}=4$, with value 6. Which conclusion about this flow is correct?
options: Not optimal: edge $(s,b)$ still has 1 unit to spare.
Optimal, as cut $\{s,a,b\}$ versus $\{t\}$ has capacity 6.
Not optimal: the cut $\{s,a\}$ versus $\{b,t\}$ allows 7.
Not optimal: 7 units can leave $s$, so 7 is reachable.

questions.question: In a maximum flow network, edge $(a,b)$ has capacity 6, and a contract requires that at least 2 units use this edge. Which bounds on $x_{ab}$ model this in the LP?
options: $2\le x_{ab}\le6$
$x_{ab}\ge2$ without an upper bound
$0\le x_{ab}\le2$

questions.question: Suppose a network had an edge from an intermediate vertex $v$ back into the source $s$, while the LP objective stayed $\max\sum_jx_{sj}$ with conservation only at vertices other than $s$ and $t$. What could go wrong?
options: Nothing, since $\sum_jx_{sj}$ still equals the flow into $t$.
Flow cycling back into $s$ via $v$ would be counted again.
The LP would become infeasible because of the extra edge.
Flow returning to $s$ would be subtracted from the objective.

questions.question: A student replaces the objective $\max\sum_jx_{sj}$ of the maximum flow LP by $\max\sum_{(i,j)}x_{ij}$, the total flow over all edges, keeping all constraints. Why is this wrong?
options: It is not wrong; conservation makes both objectives equal.
Flow on long routes or cycles is counted repeatedly.
It favours routes with few edges, since it counts edges.
It removes the capacity bounds from the model.

questions.question: A network has edges $(s,a)$ with capacity 5, $(a,t)$ 1, $(b,a)$ 3 and $(b,t)$ 4; its maximum flow is 1. If the lower bounds $x_{ij}\ge0$ were dropped from the LP, keeping $x_{ij}\le c_{ij}$ and conservation at $a$ and $b$, what optimal value would the LP report?
options: Unbounded

questions.question: A network has edges $(s,a)$ with capacity 3, $(s,b)$ 6, $(b,a)$ 2, $(a,t)$ 4 and $(b,t)$ 3; its maximum flow LP has optimal value 7. If the capacities of $(s,a)$ and $(s,b)$ are each raised by 1, what is the new optimal value?
